edges.description: Junctional membrane complexes couple sarcolemmal calcium entry to sarcoplasmic reticulum release; their disruption accompanies calcium-handling abnormalities in mutant cardiomyocytes.
Mutant mice became arrhythmogenic under catecholamine stimulation, alongside the calcium-handling defect; the arrhythmia mechanism (triggered activity or re-entry) was not resolved in the abstract.
Calcium mishandling is proposed to impair contraction and lead to dilatation under adrenergic stress in mice.

nodes.description: Homozygous knock-ins lack cardiac Bag5 protein yet are normal to 12 months and on treadmill testing. After tunicamycin they show reduced LVEF and LVFS and more apoptotic cardiomyocytes, and male knock-ins show sinus pauses. Groups were three mice per sex and genotype; apoptosis and immunoblots used one heart per group.

Knock-in mice develop ventricular dilatation, arrhythmogenicity and poor survival under catecholamine stimulation, with junctional membrane complex disruption and calcium-handling abnormalities in cardiomyocytes. AAV9 wild-type BAG5 rescues the phenotype. The exact allele and baseline phenotype are not given in the retrievable abstract.
